name: overline
purpose: Overline is the short uppercase label set above a headline to name the section, panel or group it opens (the "eyebrow"). It renders its default slot in `.text-overline-md` in the brand primary color, optionally behind a preset code-style prefix (`//`, `<>`, `</>`) and followed by a blinking terminal-style cursor. It is purely presentational text with no interaction; the marketing headers (`section-title`, `hero-title`, `call-to-action`, `media-split`, `ticker`) and several page sections render their eyebrow (the `eyebrow` prop, or `label` on `ticker`) through it.
useWhen: Name a section, panel or column group with one or two words set above its headline.
Build a custom marketing header that must match the eyebrow treatment of `section-title` and `hero-title` (the `//` prefix and the blinking cursor).
Label a band inside a page section (a comparison group, a closing panel) with the same uppercase code-style mark.
avoidWhen: The header has a headline, description and actions → use `section-title` (or `hero-title` for the hero), which already renders its `eyebrow` through Overline.
The text is a status, count or category attached to an item → use `tag` or `badge`.
The text is the heading itself → use a real heading element; Overline renders a `div` and is not a heading.
The text is a keyboard shortcut → use `kbd`.
The text is a field label → use `label`.
related: section-title` — the framed section header; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline with `prefix="//"` and `show-cursor`.
hero-title` — the hero copy block; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline closed by the cursor, with `single-line` turned off.
tag` — a compact label attached to an item, not a heading companion.
badge` — a compact count or status indicator.
bestPractices: Keep the label to one or two words: it is set uppercase and, with the default `single-line`, stays on one line whenever it fits its container.
Turn `single-line` off only when the label can be longer than its container (narrow columns, translated copy); the label then wraps under `text-pretty`, which avoids a lone word on the last line.
Use a `prefix` from the preset set only (`//`, `<>`, `</>`); the prefix is decorative and hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`), so never put meaning in it.
Use `show-cursor` for one eyebrow per view at most; the blink stops under reduced motion.
Keep the semantic heading in the element after the Overline; the Overline itself carries no heading role.

props.name: singleLine
props.doc: Keeps the prefix unbroken and the label on one line while it fits; a longer label wraps instead of overflowing.

props.name: showCursor
props.doc: Shows a blinking terminal-style cursor after the label.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: Preset prefix rendered before the label; empty renders no prefix.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The label text, rendered uppercase in the brand primary color.
